findings.text: The declared negative control does not reproduce on this host. The run's negative-control.log shows the base-revision test file reddening the later test in 20 of 20 runs under load, but 37 independent attempts here -- 10 with no load, 10 under 8 CPU-bound python loops, 7 under 40-way oversubscription, and 12 via the run's own load.py 8 -- all returned 2 passed, EXIT=0. The leak is a thread-timing race whose firing needs the earlier test's handler thread to be scheduled into the later test's patched _discover_plans_uncached; that schedule was not reachable under the load regimes I could create. The repair is sound by construction, but the guard's firing is not independently demonstrated, so the test should not be relied on to catch a reintroduction of the leak on an arbitrary host.

justifications.durability: The mechanism is sound and confirmed against the installed Python 3.14 socketserver: socket.makefile() holds a file-descriptor reference, so HTTPConnection.close() alone leaves the fd open, and ThreadingMixIn.process_request sets t.daemon = self.daemon_threads and tracks only non-daemon threads, so server_close() joins handler threads only when daemon_threads is False. The later test's assertion is unchanged. Held below full because the guard is not shown to fire independently here (see finding): the run's negative control reddens 20/20 while my 37 attempts stay green. A residual effect of daemon_threads=False is that a future test which leaves a stream open would hang server_close() rather than pass, which needs the repo's per-test bound to turn a hang into a failure.
justifications.evidence: The run's three arms exist and are internally coherent: gate-file.log (whole file, 8 passed, EXIT=0), gate-loaded.log (two tests 20x under load, passes=20 fails=0, EXIT=0) and negative-control.log (base-revision test file, passes=0 fails=20, EXIT=20, the traceback's scans list naming both the current and the earlier test's docs dir, which matches the described leak). I independently re-ran the whole file at head 65617b3f2: 8 passed in 6.00s, EXIT=0 (review-head-arm.log). Held below full because I could not reproduce the red arm in 37 independent attempts on this host; every attempt returned 2 passed, EXIT=0. The head claim reproduces; the negative control's firing does not, under my conditions.
